name: navigation
description: Moves the robot from its current location to a specified target pose within a known map, using point-to-point mobile navigation. Use this capability once a target location has already been resolved to concrete map coordinates (this capability does not perform semantic place lookup, e.g. it does not know where 'the kitchen' is; a separate planning step must resolve that to a pose first).

goal.target_pose: geometry_msgs/PoseStamped - target pose (position + orientation) the robot should navigate to, expressed in a frame that is part of the robot's TF tree (typically 'map').
goal.waypoints: geometry_msgs/PoseStamped[] - optional ordered waypoints to pass through before target_pose; empty for a direct goal.
goal.parameters_json: string - optional JSON escape hatch for stack-specific navigation parameters (e.g. behavior tree file, planner id); empty for defaults.

feedback.current_pose: geometry_msgs/PoseStamped - robot's current estimated pose while navigating.
feedback.navigation_time: builtin_interfaces/Duration - time elapsed since this navigation goal started.
feedback.estimated_time_remaining: builtin_interfaces/Duration - estimated time left to reach the goal.
feedback.number_of_recoveries: int16 - number of recovery behaviors (e.g. backing up, spinning in place) triggered so far.
feedback.distance_remaining: float32 - straight-line distance left to the goal, in meters.
feedback.current_waypoint_index: uint32 - index into the goal's waypoints array currently being pursued (0 if none/direct).

result.error_code: uint16 - 0 SUCCESS, 1 REJECTED, 2 ABORTED, 3 CANCELED, 4 TIMEOUT, 10 NO_PATH_FOUND, 11 LOCALIZATION_LOST.
result.error_msg: string - human-readable explanation, populated when error_code is non-zero.
result.final_pose: geometry_msgs/PoseStamped - robot's pose when the goal ended.
result.total_time: builtin_interfaces/Duration - total time the goal ran for.

requirements: The robot must already be localized within a known map (a valid map -> base_link transform must be available).
The target pose must be expressed in a frame that is part of the robot's TF tree.
The path between the robot and the target must only require locomotion; this capability does not open doors, use elevators, or perform any manipulation.
effects: On success (error_code == SUCCESS), the robot's physical location changes to be at (or very near) the requested target pose.
The action may trigger recovery behaviors if the robot gets stuck; these are reported via 'number_of_recoveries' in the feedback and do not require caller intervention.
A currently executing goal can be preempted by a newer navigation goal (see 'preemption' below): the previous goal is aborted and the robot starts moving toward the new target instead.

preemption.behavior_when_enabled: Sending a new goal while one is active aborts the current goal and immediately starts navigating to the new target.
preemption.behavior_when_disabled: Sending a new goal while one is active is rejected outright; the caller must wait for the current navigation to finish, or explicitly cancel it, before sending another.

navigation.allow_preemption.description: Whether a new navigation goal is allowed to preempt (replace) one that is currently executing.

navigation.mock_navigation_duration.description: Mock/simulated time it takes to complete a navigation goal. This implementation does not drive a real robot: it simulates progress over this duration for integration testing of the wider system.

navigation.mock_feedback_period.description: How often feedback is published while a goal is executing.

navigation.mock_initial_distance.description: Simulated starting distance to the goal, reported via feedback.distance_remaining and linearly decreased to 0 as the mock navigation progresses.

capabilities_file.description: Path to this very capability description file; published verbatim on /capabilities when the node is activated.

notes: This is a mock implementation, part of the EasyFleet architecture, standing in for a real navigation stack (Nav2 or otherwise) during integration testing of multi-capability systems. It does not perform real path planning, obstacle avoidance, or localization: 'current_pose' feedback simply reports the goal pose, and progress is simulated on a timer.
